title: FIPS counter incremented inside write lock is correct
description: In crypto2dev_register_provider() and crypto2dev_unregister_provider(), atomic_inc/atomic_dec_if_positive on fips_provider_count is called while holding the write_lock. This is correct: the read side in crypto2dev_lookup_algo() reads fips_provider_count under the read_lock, so the write side must update it under the write_lock to guarantee that a reader never observes a stale FIPS count relative to the provider list state. A reviewer might argue 'just use atomic_inc outside the lock — atomics are thread-safe.' That would be wrong: the issue is not atomicity of the counter increment in isolation, it is ordering relative to the list operation. If atomic_inc is called after write_unlock, a concurrent reader can see the new provider in the list but still read the old (pre-increment) fips_provider_count, causing a FIPS-only lookup to dispatch to a non-FIPS provider for one window. The write_lock serializes both the list mutation and the counter update as a single unit.
